newsitem.title: USA: Connecticut governor shrugs off gridlock fears.
newsitem.headline: Connecticut governor shrugs off gridlock fears.

text.p: Connecticut's Republican Gov. John Rowland brushed aside fears of legislative gridlock on Wednesday even though Democrats appeared to have wrested control of the state Senate.

Rowland told reporters that Republicans, who formerly held a 19-17 majority in the state Senate but lost one or two seats on Tuesday depending upon a recount, could have taken a much worse beating given President Clinton's large victory in the state.
"One of the clear messages that came through is that people like the path that we're on," said Rowland.
He said both parties in the state shared main goals, including a renewed emphasis on tax reduction, welfare and education reform and job creation.

Even though Clinton crushed Dole in Connecticut by 52 percent to 35 percent, "I didn't hear a lot of (state) Democrats running against John Rowland ... (or) against what we did for the last two years," said Rowland.

Rowland also urged Republicans around the country to learn a lesson from Clinton's re-election and change their image. "Clearly, our national party is still controlled by the right wing, and way too much influenced by some of the southerners," he said.
